correctness.rationale: Both products begin with their left word; equality forces prefix comparability, which conversely gives commutation. For the resulting strict ancestor graph, the level-constant restriction has one ancestor per earlier level and the stated factorial number of descendants per later level. For a vertex with k+1 children, weights orthogonal to the all-ones vector on children cancel the adjacency contribution at the vertex itself and all its ancestors, while each child's radial coordinates act by H_k. Nested contrast spaces are orthogonal by levelwise cancellation; disjoint subtrees are orthogonal by support. Completeness can be checked at each absolute depth j: if N_d=n!/(n−d)!, the dimensions at that depth add to 1+Σ_{d<j}N_d(n−d−1)=1+Σ_{d<j}(N_{d+1}−N_d)=N_j. The restrictions are self-adjoint in the positive weights k!/(k−i)! on the levels. For M=H_k+I the last two rows and columns coincide. In the leading k-square minor, differencing successive rows produces pivots k−1 through 1 and a last first-column entry 1, hence determinant (−1)^(k−1)(k−1)!. All principal cofactors vanish except the two equal ones at the endpoints of the identical pair. This gives P'_k(−1)=−2(k−1)! and telescoping exponents give n!. The k=1 minor is [1]. For n≥2 the empty word alone is central; deleting it partitions the graph by first letter into n copies of the smaller graph.
residual_risks: The finite symbolic checks in the original are supplementary. The decomposition need not give distinct eigenvalues across different blocks; −1 is simple within each block, not within the whole adjacency operator.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general join recurrence covers computation of this entire characteristic polynomial. Complete binary closures do not have the decreasing level branching here. The general scalar recurrence is not a statement of the invariant sibling-by-depth modes or their operators. Those modes do extend naturally to level-regular ancestor closures; that generalization alone is not prior coverage.

evidence: For Γ_n=K_1 joined to n copies of Γ_(n−1), the general prior formula specializes to χ_n=χ_(n−1)^n·[z−n r_(n−1)(z)]. The all-ones resolvent is radial; applying the scalar join Schur complement on depth-value coordinates gives the bracket P_n/P_(n−1), with P_0=z. Iteration gives the frozen factor exponents. The older T_m proof splits constants and Laplacian copy modes, not the adjacency radial contrasts.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the polynomial as covered by a routine specialization, not just as numerically computable. The scalar factor identity has no eigenspace information. The stated orthogonal vertex-indexed spaces identify where the adjacency operator acts by each quotient and how to build modes; the block simplicity and exact derivative are established separately rather than inferred from prior total multiplicity.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct contribution is the explicit orthogonal adjacency decomposition into depthwise sibling modes with identified factorial-sized quotient entries and block multiplicities, and the simple-root derivative for each radial block. The prefix graph itself occurs in older work; the bulk characteristic polynomial is recoverable algebraically from a prior trivially perfect graph recursion, and the whole-graph −1 count is covered by general cograph multiplicity results. Neither bare spectral computability nor the whole-graph −1 count is independent novelty.
residual_risks: Full-text retrieval for targeted related Bethe-tree results was unsuccessful; a general level-regular ancestor-closure adjacency mode theorem, if found, could subsume the structural claim. No such source was established by the inspected material.

checked_sources: Frozen RESULT.md Steps 2–3; comparison with prior join polynomial and Laplacian recursion
value.rationale: The orthogonal block spaces identify actual adjacency modes, not only a factorization or an eigenvalue count. They give a constructive eigenfunction reduction from a graph with factorially many vertices to depth quotients of size at most n+1 and locate each copy at a specific prefix with levelwise cancellation. This is useful for adjacency representation and eigenfunction questions where a characteristic polynomial or a congruence algorithm cannot recover the modes. The analysis of −1 within each radial block further identifies how that repeated eigenvalue is assembled.
residual_risks: Value is structural; neither polynomial computability nor the prior-covered whole-graph −1 count alone would support this verdict.
